text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- The Finnish Science Academy will start a study programme next year on the causes and consequences of economic depression in the 1990's.
- Members of the Social Democratic Party are unsatisfied with party's achievements in government, a poll by MTV shows.
- Six months of military service is not long enough, says Aapo Saari, director of the Finnish Reservist Federation, commenting on a plan to cut the service time.
- Forty-one percent of mutual insurer Suomi's representatives due to meet on Tuesday approve Pohjola's plan to take it over and 25 percent reject the plan, poll shows.
- Electronics sub-contactors suffer from falling profits and low prices, industry says.
- The rise in flat prices is levelling out and possibly even curbing, real estate agents say.
- German builders still employ many Finnish construction companies, says Jarmo Lindell, director of the Finnish export center in Berlin.
- Many break-away cooperative banks in northern Savo consider returning to the OKOBANK group.
- A majority of trade union leaders have a wait-and-see attitude in the EMU discussion, a poll shows.
